description:
Schloss Neustadt-Glewe, a Dutch Baroque palace in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern's Ludwigslust-Parchim district, was built between 1619 and 1717 and has survived more than four centuries of upheaval. Its interior is distinguished by an extraordinary expanse of decorative stucco — over 1,600 square meters in total, created by Italian masters over eight years — with 32 fireplaces individually adorned with cornices, rosettes and stucco figures. This Baroque "New Castle" (Neues Schloss) is a genuinely separate structure from the town's older Alte Burg, a medieval castle dating to around 1250 that survives as its own distinct local landmark.

Today the palace operates as a hotel with 37 rooms across three categories, including three suites — the Standard rooms housed in an ancillary building just a few meters from the main structure, and the Superior rooms within the main Baroque building itself. The property recently changed ownership, with the new owner planning a comprehensive renovation; recent guest reviews note the hotel is no longer rated at its previous 4-star standard and have flagged occasional service gaps, though it remains open and actively bookable, with over 1,600 verified Booking.com reviews and a 7.9/10 rating as of this writing.

The distinction between the Neues Schloss and the town's Alte Burg is worth stating clearly for anyone researching Neustadt-Glewe online: the two structures are entirely separate buildings with different construction dates, architectural styles and histories, sharing only their location in the same small Mecklenburg town. The Alte Burg, a genuine medieval fortification from around 1250, functions as a local museum, distinct from the Baroque palace covered here.

The eight-year stucco program that decorated the palace's interior represents a substantial artistic investment for a rural Mecklenburg residence, reflecting the considerable resources the ducal patrons of the period were willing to commit to interior decoration during the palace's roughly century-long construction period.

The palace's ownership transition and planned renovation reflect a genuinely active, ongoing chapter in the property's history rather than a settled status quo — prospective guests should expect the property to be in a period of change, with service standards and star ratings potentially shifting as the new ownership implements its plans.

The Lewitz nature reserve and the wider Mecklenburg Lake District surrounding Neustadt-Glewe give the area a genuinely scenic, water-rich rural character, and nearby Ludwigslust Palace offers guests a further grand Baroque and Neoclassical counterpoint within easy driving distance.

Mecklenburg's dense concentration of ducal palaces and water castles, of which Neustadt-Glewe is one example among several covered in this collection, reflects the region's history as a patchwork of small aristocratic territories, each historically maintaining its own seat of residence even within a relatively compact geographic area.

faqs.question: Is Neustadt-Glewe Palace the same as the town's Alte Burg?
faqs.answer: No. The Alte Burg is a separate medieval castle dating to around 1250, a distinct building with no connection to the Baroque Neues Schloss (New Castle) covered here, which was built between 1619 and 1717.

faqs.question: Is Neustadt-Glewe Palace still open given the recent ownership change?
faqs.answer: Yes — the hotel remains open and actively bookable in 2026, with over 1,600 verified Booking.com reviews, though recent guest reviews note it is no longer rated at its previous 4-star standard as the new ownership plans a comprehensive renovation.

faqs.question: Are all the rooms within the main palace building?
faqs.answer: No — Standard rooms are in an ancillary building a few metres from the main structure, while Superior rooms and suites are within the main Baroque palace building itself.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** About 20 minutes by car from Ludwigslust; roughly 40 minutes from Schwerin and 1h15 from Hamburg.

**Rooms & rates:** 37 rooms in 3 categories (including 3 suites) — Standard rooms in a nearby ancillary building, Superior rooms within the main Baroque palace building itself. From €106/night.

**On-site:** Vaulted restaurant, bar, sauna, 3 event rooms.

**Good to know:** New ownership and a planned full renovation mean the guest experience may be in transition — worth checking current reviews for the latest state before booking.

**Combine with:** Ludwigslust Palace and the Mecklenburg Lake District, both a short drive away.
